13.0.s.en: (4) The punishment of the surrounding nations and their repentance

13.0.0.en: Girdle: the undergarment worn around the waist that covers the thighs.

13.0.1.en: God wanted to show the pride of His people, which caused them the affliction of captivity, so He gave them this parable. He asked Jeremiah to buy himself a linen girdle, which is a symbol of purity and was the clothing of the priests; that is, God gave His people purity and a life of righteousness, but they rejected them. And He asked him not to wash it in water, since it was new and did not need this washing; this signifies that God clothed them with righteousness and did not leave them in need of anything. In addition, washing in water makes the girdle lose its firmness, so that it becomes slack and does not do its work well in covering the body tightly; that is, God kept them from every weakness.

13.1.1.en: God asked Jeremiah to take the new linen girdle that he had bought. This signifies the righteousness that God's people obtained and which clung to them as clothes cling to the body, and his buying it means that he took care to acquire it and God granted it to him. He took this girdle and traveled to the river Euphrates in Iraq, a long distance of about 350 miles from Jerusalem, and buried this girdle in a hole of the rock and covered it with earth. This signifies Babylon's humiliation of God's people and their captivity there, because they had spoiled the righteousness of God given to them through their pride and their worship of idols.

13.1.2.en: The rock signifies their human strength and their reliance on their pride and stubbornness. Jeremiah traveled the first time to the Euphrates and back, 700 miles, and the second time, in the following verses, he also traveled to the Euphrates, about 700 miles again; so he traveled 1,400 miles to show the hardship that God's people would meet in captivity, when they were transported from their cities to the land of Babylon.

13.2.0.en: After many days: after a period that may have been several months.

13.2.1.en: After a period God asked Jeremiah to travel to the Euphrates and take out the linen girdle that he had buried in the hole of the rock. He did as the LORD commanded him, and dug and took out the buried girdle, and found it spoiled, not fit to be worn or used for anything. This signifies the loss of the dignity and righteousness of God's people when they worshiped idols and were proud, so they lost their holiness, their dignity and their nationhood, and Babylon scattered them in the lands of its kingdom, because they had forsaken God.

13.3.0.en: God declared His purpose in this parable, that He would mar the pride of His people dwelling in the kingdom of Judah and its capital Jerusalem by the Babylonian captivity.

13.4.0.en: And just as the linen girdle was spoiled, so the dignity of God's people will be spoiled, because they worshiped idols and relied on them in pride.

13.5.0.en: God rebukes His people with sorrow, showing His great love for them, for He had caused them to cleave to Himself as a people of their own, bringing them out of the land of Egypt, keeping them in the wilderness, bringing them into the Promised Land and dwelling in their midst, as is shown by the parable of the girdle that cleaves to the body; but sadly they rejected God and were spoiled and entered into humiliation at the hand of Babylon.

13.5.1.en: Pride is the root of all evils. So if you sin, return to God with humility, lowliness and repentance, and do not lean on your abilities and intelligence, but confess your fault before God and apologize to others, and He will forgive you and lift every affliction from you, and you will regain your peace.

13.5.3.en: 12- Therefore thou shalt speak unto them this word; Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Every bottle shall be filled with wine: and they shall say unto thee, Do we not certainly know that every bottle shall be filled with wine? 13- Then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit upon David's throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.

13.5.4.en: 14- And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the LORD: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.

13.6.0.en: Bottle: a vessel of skin in which wine or liquids are put.

13.6.1.en: The second parable that God gives His people so that they may repent is that every bottle shall be filled with wine. They were accustomed to filling their bottles with wine and keeping it and drinking from it in their houses, so God chose this parable, familiar in their life; and they answered Jeremiah when he said this to them that he had added little, because we know that every bottle we fill with wine we keep in our houses. Thus they understood only the literal meaning, because they were superficial and proud and had no spiritual understanding, so they did not understand that their lives had been filled, like the bottle, with the desires into which they had plunged, and with which they were drunk, that is, they had lost their minds and discernment, and had become like animals in their lusts, and worshiped statues and forsook God, the true God.

13.7.0.en: Since they did not understand the meaning of the parable, God explained it to them by the mouth of Jeremiah: that God had left them to their desires and abandoned them because of their pride, the people and their leaders, the kings, prophets and priests, who had lost their discernment like drunkards.

13.8.0.en: Because of their immersion in desires and their rejection of God, He allows Babylon to dash them, great and small, and God does not have mercy on them because they persist in their sins.

13.8.1.en: Beware of too many occupations, for they will gradually draw you away from God and then quietly lead you into sin without your noticing, until you are immersed in it because you have left God and lost your protection. Hold to a spiritual rule in your prayers and your readings every day, in addition to your confession and your Communion; by these four you will find your way of salvation in the midst of the world.

13.8.3.en: 15- Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the LORD hath spoken. 16- Give glory to the LORD your God, before he cause darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains, and, while ye look for light, he turn it into the shadow of death, and make it gross darkness.

13.8.4.en: 17- But if ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for your pride; and mine eye shall weep sore, and run down with tears, because the LORD's flock is carried away captive. 18- Say unto the king and to the queen, Humble yourselves, sit down: for your principalities shall come down, even the crown of your glory. 19- The cities of the south shall be shut up, and none shall open them: Judah shall be carried away captive all of it, it shall be wholly carried away captive. 20- Lift up your eyes, and behold them that come from the north: where is the flock that was given thee, thy beautiful flock?

13.8.5.en: 21- What wilt thou say when he shall punish thee? for thou hast taught them to be captains, and as chief over thee: shall not sorrows take thee, as a woman in travail?

13.9.0.en: Jeremiah calls his people to humble themselves and so to listen attentively to the word of God, who calls them to repentance; and if they reject His voice, destruction will come upon them.

13.9.1.en: When you read the Holy Bible or listen to a sermon, be humble and let the word of God keep you, judge you and guide you, so that you understand God's word and His message to you, and your life is changed, and you rescue yourself from destruction and obtain the mercy of God.

13.10.0.en: Jeremiah calls them to worship God, glorify His name and thank Him for His kindnesses, so that they do not ascribe glory to themselves or to the pagan gods.

13.10.1.en: And if they do not glorify God, they will stray further from the way of God, lost in their pride, which he likens to mountains; and because their pride leads them astray, he calls them the dark mountains, that is, their hideous pride, which hides from them the sight of God and the hearing of His voice. While they wait for guidance and rescue from their afflictions, their straying and immersion in base desires and the worship of idols increase, so they advance toward their destruction from a straying that he calls “gross darkness,” and their drawing near to destruction he calls “the shadow of death.” All this is the result of pride; for when they relied on their intelligence and their formal worship, and thought it a light that would guide them, they did not find it, but walked toward the destruction that was accomplished at the hand of Babylon.

13.11.0.en: Jeremiah warns them that if they do not listen to the voice of God and repent, destruction will befall them at the hand of Babylon, and because of this expected destruction Jeremiah will weep for them; and because no one understands the word of God, he will weep in secret places, because he is certain that the people of God, that is, His flock, will be taken captive to Babylon and many of them will be killed.

13.12.0.en: Then God asks Jeremiah to address his words to the young king Jehoiachin and to his mother the queen, who was involved in the administration of government, that they humble themselves and repent, because after a little while the king would be taken captive and the crown would be taken from his head, he and his mother, and they would carry him to Babylon; and this was done in 598 B.C.

13.13.0.en: When the Babylonians attacked, they besieged Jerusalem and cut it off from the other southern cities of Judah, so that these could not come to its aid.

13.14.0.en: God addresses Jerusalem as a woman and says to her: Behold the armies of Babylon coming from the north to attack you and take your people captive, whom He calls the flock of your glory, since you relied on these children of yours; so where are they? The Babylonians have taken possession of your cities and seized your great men and sent them to Babylon.

13.15.0.en: Then God calls to Jerusalem and says to her: What will you do when the armies of Babylon punish her with destruction, devastation, killing and captivity? And at her surrender, rulers from Babylon will be set over her to humiliate her and all who remain in her, as a woman in travail suffers when the hour of her delivery draws near.

13.15.2.en: 22- And if thou say in thine heart, Wherefore come these things upon me? For the greatness of thine iniquity are thy skirts discovered, and thy heels made bare. 23- Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil. 24- Therefore will I scatter them as the stubble that passeth away by the wind of the wilderness. 25- This is thy lot, the portion of thy measures from me, saith the LORD; because thou hast forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood. 26- Therefore will I discover thy skirts upon thy face, that thy shame may appear. 27- I have seen thine adulteries, and thy neighings, the lewdness of thy whoredom, and thine abominations on the hills in the fields. Woe unto thee, O Jerusalem! wilt thou not be made clean? when shall it once be?

13.16.1.en: Thy skirts: the hems of your garment.

13.16.3.en: Thy heels: the feet from behind.

13.16.4.en: Jerusalem asks, after the Babylonians have destroyed her, saying: Why has this destruction come upon me? And God answers her, saying: Because of your evil desires the Babylonians struck you, which is expressed by the lifting of the skirts of the garment, so that Jerusalem's nakedness appears, that is, she becomes desolate; and this devastation was accomplished against your will, because the power of Babylon was great. This also points to Jerusalem's depravity and her adultery after pagan worship, so he uses these expressions, which show that she walked in the way of adultery and so was laid waste at the hand of Babylon, like a woman whose nakedness was exposed in adultery; likewise she was laid waste as a city with everything in her.

13.17.0.en: The Ethiopian: the Abyssinian, black in color.

13.17.1.en: His spots: the black dots and the stripes on the skin of the leopard.

13.17.2.en: People are accustomed to say that the wicked man will not change his evil once he is used to it, and cannot leave evil, like the black African who cannot change his skin and make it another color, and likewise the leopard cannot change its striped skin full of black dots. But God opens the door of His mercies and calls His people to leave their evils, and God will lift from them all these afflictions of which He spoke, that is, the captivity and what follows it.

13.18.0.en: But if the people of God persist in their evil, God will scatter them as the wind scatters the stubble in the empty desert; so He will scatter them in the kingdom of Babylon and take them far from their land.

13.19.0.en: Of thy measures: from “measure,” a vessel used to gauge volumes, such as the liter.

13.19.1.en: God says that the portion of Jerusalem and Judea is captivity and scattering, and God allows Babylon to do this as a punishment for His people for a certain period until they repent, and then He brings them back from captivity; and the cause of these evils is Jerusalem's trust in the false pagan gods.

13.20.0.en: God repeats that He will allow the devastation of Jerusalem, which He likens to the uncovering of a woman's nakedness by lifting the skirt of her garment, so that her face is covered and her nakedness appears, that is, Jerusalem loses all understanding and sight and becomes desolate.

13.21.0.en: Thine adulteries: the various kinds of adultery in which you walked.

13.21.1.en: Thy neighings: the sound of the horse.

13.21.3.en: Thine abominations: the statues of the pagan gods, which God hates.

13.21.4.en: God shows the cause of Jerusalem's devastation, namely her immersion in adultery after foreign gods and her running like the animal, which He represents by the neighing, after the desires of adultery, whether physical adultery or attachment to the worship of idols; and adultery was committed on the hills and in the fields, where they offered this adultery as worship of idols and as immersion in their desires. And God marvels at Jerusalem's persistence in adultery and her distance from Him, and calls to her in sorrow: How long will you refuse purity and the pure life with God?

13.21.5.en: If you fall into evil, return quickly to God in repentance and do not reject His voice that calls you, lest you enter into many afflictions and He forsake you and you hasten to your own destruction. He loves you, so do not harden your heart or reject His love.

14.0.0.en: The LORD spoke to Jeremiah about a drought that would come upon the kingdom of Judah, that it might lead them to repentance; this was the drought that occurred in the days of King Jehoiakim, before the armies of Babylon attacked and took them captive.

14.0.1.en: Judah mourneth: He portrays the kingdom of Judah as a woman weeping because of the lack of water, thirst, the drying up of the crops and the death of the beasts.

14.0.2.en: The gates thereof languish: the cities of Judah suffered thirst and hunger and their sons went out from them, so the gates no longer had value in protecting or fortifying those in the city, as a flower withers and becomes useless. They are black unto the ground: the affliction on the people of Judah increased, so they were in great sorrow and bowed their heads to the ground, and their strength weakened, so they fell to the ground from thirst and hunger.

14.0.3.en: The cry of Jerusalem is gone up: from the severity of thirst and hunger the people cried out everywhere.

14.1.0.en: Their little ones: their servants, those who work for them.

14.1.1.en: Pits: pools and gatherings of water.

14.1.2.en: The rich and the great sent those who work for them, or their servants, with vessels to fill them with water from any place, but they found all the gatherings of water dried up, so they returned in shame and disgrace to these great men, and from the intensity of shame they covered their heads and bowed them to the ground.

14.2.0.en: Not only did the great suffer from thirst, but also the poor, who are the farmers working the land, because it was cracked from dryness and the lack of rain, so they were ashamed, and therefore covered their heads.

14.3.0.en: The hind: the female deer, a kind of swift-running gazelle.

14.3.2.en: The hind left her natural place, which is the forests, because the earth dried up and the plants died; and when she found her young she found no water for them to drink or food of grass for them to eat, so she left them to die and went to look for water and food.

14.4.0.en: The wild asses: the wild donkey.

14.4.1.en: Dragons: predatory animals, larger than the fox and smaller than the wolf.

14.4.2.en: The wild donkey found no food, so it went up on the hills and the plateaus to search for food, and from running it grew tired and breathed with difficulty and needed to snuff up the wind lest it die of weakness, hunger and thirst, like the jackals that run and pant; and from the leanness of the wild asses their sight failed.

14.4.3.en: Your distance from the source of the waters of grace, that is, the Holy Spirit working in the Church, weakens your spirit and exposes you to many troubles, so that you almost die and become an easy prey for Satan, falling into many sins. So submit to Him, hold to His commandments and abide in His Church, and you will regain your strength.

14.5.0.en: The prophet Jeremiah bears the sins of his people and offers this prayer, confessing on their behalf and on behalf of his own weakness that they have sinned against God and their iniquities are many, which testify that they are wicked and deserve punishment such as this drought; but their hope is in the love of God, who has mercy on them, because His name is called upon them, for they are His people, so with the boldness of a son he asks God's mercy.

14.5.1.en: God is your heavenly Father; He rejoices in your taking refuge in Him, so ask Him earnestly to have mercy on you, support you, rescue you from every affliction and give you repentance. Trust in your sonship to Him, so that you speak to Him with the boldness of sons; and if He does not answer quickly, know that He is concerned with your prayer and will rescue you in the end.

14.6.0.en: He pleads with God and says to Him: Why have You left us in the drought and humiliation and become like a stranger to us, like a traveler who lodges in the desert? He asks Him to enter their cities and rescue them, because they are His people and He is their only hope in their afflictions.

14.7.0.en: He continues to ask God to rescue them and says: Why do You stand silent and not stretch out Your hand to have mercy on us, as if You were bewildered and did not know how to rescue us, though You are mighty and able to do all things? You are in our midst and are our God, so do not leave us in our affliction but rescue us.

14.8.0.en: God was grieved at His people's lack of steadfastness in living with Him and worshiping in Jerusalem, for they moved about in many places on the hills and in the fields to worship the idols that they had set up there... Therefore He calls them “this people” and not “My people,” and even threatens them that He sees their sins and will punish them for them.

14.9.0.en: In the face of the persistence of God's people in their sins, the prophet's prayers or any intercession will not profit them; therefore God says to him with sorrow: Do not pray for them, because they have not yet repented, and I will not lift from them the punishment that I have allowed, that perhaps they may repent.

14.10.0.en: God also decides, as a result of His people's persistence in the worship of idols and in evil worship, that He rejects their prayers as well as their sacrifices and offerings to Him, because they are without repentance, and He declares that He will punish them with kinds of punishment, which are:

14.10.1.en: 1- The sword, that is, killing, which was accomplished when the armies of Babylon attacked.

14.10.2.en: 2- Famine, which was accomplished in the days of King Jehoiakim, as mentioned in this chapter.

14.10.3.en: 3- Pestilence, by the spread of various diseases among them.

14.10.4.en: Do not justify your sins, because this makes you persist in them and lose God's forgiveness; rather various afflictions come upon you, which God allows out of His love for you, since by them He calls you to repentance. For if you forget God, God allows you material afflictions because you have become attached to material things, and when you lose your hope in them you return in repentance and feel the importance of spiritual things, so you hold to them and find your way toward eternity.

14.11.0.en: Jeremiah makes an excuse for his people before God, that the cause of their persistence in evil is the deception of the false prophets, who promised them peace and material comfort and did not direct them to repentance.

14.12.0.en: God declares that He did not send the false prophets and that all they claim of visions and divination is a lie and vain, worthless talk, so that the people may know the truth about the false prophets through the mouth of Jeremiah and return in repentance to God.

14.13.0.en: God declares His punishment of these false prophets, that He will allow them to be killed and the rest to suffer from hunger, so that their evil comes upon their own heads; for they prophesied that neither sword nor famine would come, so sword and famine will come first upon them.

14.14.0.en: Then, after punishing the prophets, God will also punish the people who followed them and rejected God and did not repent, and He will punish them also with the sword and famine.

14.14.1.en: Do not be careless in your speech, lest you fall into the sin of lying and deceive others, for God is looking at you and is just, and He will punish you because you fell into lying and caused another to stumble; so hasten to repentance and you will obtain His mercies.

14.15.0.en: God forbade the prophet to pray for the people because they refuse to repent, but His fatherhood makes Him grieve over them, so He calls the prophet to weep continually over them and likens the kingdom of Judah to a virgin, that is, a weak girl, whom the wicked attacked and shattered, and He declares clearly that the blow of Babylon that will fall upon her is a bitter blow, that is, very hard; perhaps the people will hear the words of Jeremiah and cease from their sins.

14.16.0.en: As a result of Babylon's attack many will be killed and thrown out in the fields, and those who hid in the cities will sicken from hunger, because Babylon besieges their cities and keeps food and drink from them. As for the leaders of the people, the priests and the false prophets, their inability to rescue the people will be revealed, and they will go about the land in bewilderment and helplessness; indeed the Babylonians will carry them to another land, where they will go about in shame and the humiliation of slavery.

14.17.0.en: The prophet pleads, interceding for his people, and speaks to God to rescue them from this blow, and with the boldness of sonship he rebukes them in love, saying: Why have You rejected Your kingdom Judah and Your city Zion, which is the old name of Jerusalem? Your people still beseech You, asking for healing from this blow and for peace to return to them after this decision. The lie of the prophets has been revealed, who claimed that nothing would befall Jerusalem and Judah since the temple of God was in them, and that the kingdom of Israel was taken captive by Assyria because it was far from Jerusalem; thus they deceived the people and did not lead them to repentance.

14.18.0.en: Jeremiah confesses on behalf of his people that they have sinned against God and continued in the evils their fathers did.

14.18.1.en: If you are a father or a mother or a servant, pray for those you shepherd, and prostrate yourself and plead with God for them, offering the tears of repentance for them, because the weakness of your care caused them these sins.

14.19.0.en: Jeremiah pleads with God for his people, not for their righteousness but for His goodness, and reminds Him of three things to move His heart toward them, which are:

14.19.1.en: 1- God's name, which means His mercy and perfection; for because they are His people who believed in Him, He forgives them and lifts the affliction from them; and this shows the prophet's fatherhood toward his people.

14.19.2.en: 2- The throne of God's glory, which is His temple in which He dwelt and which was filled with the prayers of many godly people through the ages; so although the people are unworthy, God has compassion on them because they repent.

14.19.3.en: 3- God's covenant, which He made with the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; so for the sake of God's mercies and goodness He lifts the afflictions from them.

14.20.1.en: The vanities of the Gentiles: the pagan gods.

14.20.2.en: The prophet declares his faith that God alone is able to lift the drought by sending down rain, and so rescue His people from hunger and death, while the pagan gods are statues, unable to do anything.

14.20.3.en: God disciplines His people and supports His prophet

14.20.5.en: 1- Then said the LORD unto me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind could not be toward this people: cast them out of my sight, and let them go forth. 2- And it shall come to pass, if they say unto thee, Whither shall we go forth? then thou shalt tell them, Thus saith the LORD; Such as are for death, to death; and such as are for the sword, to the sword; and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for the captivity, to the captivity. 3- And I will appoint over them four kinds, saith the LORD: the sword to slay, and the dogs to tear, and the fowls of the heaven, and the beasts of the earth, to devour and destroy. 4- And I will cause them to be removed into all kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem. 5- For who shall have pity upon thee, O Jerusalem? or who shall bemoan thee? or who shall go aside to ask how thou doest? 6- Thou hast forsaken me, saith the LORD, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting. 7- And I will fan them with a fan in the gates of the land; I will bereave them of children, I will destroy my people, since they return not from their ways. 8- Their widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas: I have brought upon them against the mother of the young men a spoiler at noonday: I have caused him to fall upon it suddenly, and terrors upon the city. 9- She that hath borne seven languisheth: she hath given up the ghost; her sun is gone down while it was yet day: she hath been ashamed and confounded: and the residue of them will I deliver to the sword before their enemies, saith the LORD.
